title.raw: 卷三十三 志第二十三 五行四 Volume 33 Treatises 23: Five Elements 4

sentences.zh: 志第二十三 五行四

translations.literal: Treatises 23: Five Elements 4.
translations.idiomatic: Treatises 23: The Five Elements, Part Four.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。

translations.literal: The "Tradition of the Five Elements" says: "If one abbreviates the ancestral temples, does not pray and offer sacrifice, abolishes sacrifices, and goes against the season's timing, then water will not moisten downward."
translations.idiomatic: The "Tradition of the Five Elements" states: "When the ruler curtails the ancestral temples, neglects prayer and sacrifice, abandons the rites of worship, and defies the seasons, water ceases to flow downward as it should."

sentences.zh: 」謂水失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: " This means that water loses its nature and becomes a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " That is, water abandons its proper nature and disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「聽之不聰，是謂不謀。

translations.literal: It also says: "If hearing is not keen, this is called lack of counsel."
translations.idiomatic: It further says: "When hearing fails, that is called want of deliberation."

sentences.zh: 厥咎急，厥罰恆寒，厥極貧。

translations.literal: Its fault is haste; its punishment is constant cold; its ultimate limit is poverty.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is rashness; the penalty is unending cold; the extreme is destitution.

sentences.zh: 時則有鼓妖，時則有魚孽，時則有豕禍，時則有耳屙，時則有黑眚、黑祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are drum prodigies; at such times calamities of fish; at such times pig disasters; at such times ear excretions; at such times black disasters and black portents.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons one finds ominous drums, plagues involving fish, calamities involving swine, disorders of the ears, and black disasters and black omens.

sentences.zh: 惟火沴水。

translations.literal: Only fire harms water.
translations.idiomatic: Only fire can injure water.

sentences.zh: 」魚孽，劉歆傳以為介蟲之孽，謂蝗屬也。

translations.literal: " As for fish calamities, Liu Xin's tradition takes them as calamities of armored creatures, meaning locusts and the like.
translations.idiomatic: " Fish calamities, in Liu Xin's tradition, are classified as calamities of shelled creatures—that is, locusts and their kind.

sentences.zh: 水不潤下：

translations.literal: Water not moistening downward:
translations.idiomatic: When water fails to moisten downward:

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年六月，大雨霖，伊、洛溢至津陽城門，漂數千家，流殺人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, great rains poured in succession; the Yi and Luo overflowed to the Jinyang city gate, sweeping away several thousand households and drowning people in the current.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Huangchu, under Emperor Wen of Wei, torrential rains fell without cease. The Yi and Luo rivers rose until they reached the Jinyang city gate, carrying off thousands of homes and drowning people in the flood.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位，自鄴遷洛，營造宮室，而不起宗廟，太祖神主猶在鄴。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor took the throne, he moved from Ye to Luoyang and built palaces, yet did not erect the ancestral temple; the spirit tablets of Emperor Taizu still remained in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, he moved the capital from Ye to Luoyang and began building palaces, yet he never established the ancestral temple. The spirit tablets of Emperor Taizu still remained in Ye.

sentences.zh: 嘗於建始殿饗祭如家人之禮，終黃初不復還鄴，而圓丘、方澤、南北郊、社、稷等神位，未有定所。

translations.literal: He once offered sacrifices at the Jianshi Hall in the manner of a family feast; through the entire Huangchu era he never returned to Ye, while the Round Mound, Square Pond, southern and northern suburbs, altars of soil and grain, and other divine seats had no fixed locations.
translations.idiomatic: He once performed sacrifices at the Jianshi Hall in the informal manner of a household feast. Throughout the Huangchu period he never returned to Ye, and the Round Mound, Square Pond, southern and northern suburban altars, and the altars of soil and grain had no established sites.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟，廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for abbreviating the ancestral temples and abolishing sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for curtailing the ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「顓事者知，誅罰絕理，厥災水。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "The obstinate in affairs are wise; punishments cut off principle—its calamity is water."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "Those who fixate on their own affairs fancy themselves wise; when punishments sever all principle, the calamity is water."

sentences.zh: 其水也，雨殺人已隕霜，大風天黃。

translations.literal: As for its water: rain kills people; frost has already fallen; great winds; the sky turns yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Its manifestation in water: rain that kills, frost that has already fallen, great winds, and a sky turned yellow.

sentences.zh: 饑而不損，茲謂泰。

translations.literal: Famine yet no reduction—this is called excess.
translations.idiomatic: Famine yet no relief—this is called overreaching.

sentences.zh: 厥災水殺人。

translations.literal: Its calamity: water kills people.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity: water that kills.

sentences.zh: 避遏有德，茲謂狂。

translations.literal: Avoiding and obstructing the virtuous—this is called madness.
translations.idiomatic: Shunning and blocking the worthy—this is called frenzy.

sentences.zh: 厥災水，水流殺人也；

translations.literal: Its calamity is water; flowing water kills people;
translations.idiomatic: The calamity is water—floods that drown;

sentences.zh: 已水則地生蟲。

translations.literal: when water has passed, the earth breeds insects.
translations.idiomatic: once the waters recede, insects spring from the earth.

sentences.zh: 歸獄不解，茲謂追非。

translations.literal: Returning prisoners not released—this is called pursuing wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sent back but not freed—this is called clinging to error.

sentences.zh: 厥水寒殺人。

translations.literal: Its water: cold kills people.
translations.idiomatic: Its water: killing cold.

sentences.zh: 追誅不解，茲謂不理。

translations.literal: Pursuing punishments without release—this is called lack of order.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless pursuit of punishment—this is called disorder.

sentences.zh: 厥水五穀不收。

translations.literal: Its water: the five grains are not harvested.
translations.idiomatic: Its water: crop failure.

sentences.zh: 大敗不解，茲謂皆陰。

translations.literal: Great defeat without resolution—this is called all yin.
translations.idiomatic: Great defeat without remedy—this is called total yin dominance.

sentences.zh: 厥水流入國邑，隕霜殺穀。」

translations.literal: Its water flows into the capital and districts; falling frost kills the grain."
translations.idiomatic: Its water floods the capital and towns; frost destroys the crops."

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏八年夏，茶陵縣鴻水溢出，流漂二百餘家；

translations.literal: In summer of the eighth year of Chiwu under Sun Quan of Wu, the great flood at Chaling County overflowed, sweeping away more than two hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year of Chiwu, under Sun Quan of Wu, a great flood burst forth in Chaling County and carried off more than two hundred households;

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，丹陽故鄣等縣又鴻水溢。

translations.literal: In autumn of the thirteenth year, Danyang Guzhang and other counties again saw the great flood overflow.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, Danyang, Guzhang, and other counties were flooded again.

sentences.zh: 案權稱帝三十年，竟不於建業創七廟，但有父堅一廟，遠在長沙，而郊禋禮禮闕。

translations.literal: Examining the case: Quan had styled himself emperor for thirty years, yet never established the seven temples at Jianye; he had only one temple to his father Jian, far away in Changsha, while suburban and border sacrifices were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: On examination: Quan had held the imperial title for thirty years yet never established the seven ancestral temples at Jianye. He maintained only a single temple to his father Sun Jian, far off in Changsha, while the suburban and border rites were neglected entirely.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾初，群臣奏宜效祀，又弗許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiahe, the ministers submitted that he should perform the suburban sacrifices, but again he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiahe era, his ministers urged him to perform the suburban sacrifices, but once again he refused.

sentences.zh: 末年雖一南郊，而北郊遂無聞焉。

translations.literal: In his later years he performed the southern suburb once, but the northern suburb was never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Late in his reign he did perform the southern suburban sacrifice once, but the northern suburban rite was never undertaken.

sentences.zh: 且三江、五湖、衡、霍、會稽，皆吳、楚之望，亦不見秩，反禮羅陽妖神，以求福助。

translations.literal: Moreover the Three Rivers, Five Lakes, Heng, Huo, and Kuaiji—all altars of Wu and Chu—also received no ranked sacrifices; instead he honored the demon gods of Luoyang to seek blessing and aid.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rivers, Five Lakes, Mount Heng, Mount Huo, and Kuaiji—all great altars of Wu and Chu—likewise received no proper offerings. Instead he paid ritual honor to demonic spirits of Luoyang in hope of blessing.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，權簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，示此罰，欲其感悟也。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seemed to say that Quan abbreviated the ancestral temples, did not pray and sacrifice, and abolished worship—showing this punishment to make him awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent seemed to say that Quan had curtailed the ancestral temples, neglected prayer and sacrifice, and abandoned worship—and sent this punishment to stir him to repentance.

sentences.zh: 太元元年，又有大風湧水之異。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixuan, there were again anomalies of great winds and surging water.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taixuan, great winds and surging floods appeared once more.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權南郊，疑是鑒咎征乎？

translations.literal: That winter Quan performed the southern suburb—was this perhaps taking warning from the signs of blame?
translations.idiomatic: That winter Quan performed the southern suburban sacrifice—was he perhaps heeding the warning signs?

sentences.zh: 還而寢疾。

translations.literal: On returning he fell ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and took to his bed with illness.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month, he died.

sentences.zh: 一曰，權時信納譖訴，雖陸議勳重，子和儲貳，猶不得其終。

translations.literal: One view says: in Quan's time he trusted and accepted slander; though Lu Xun's merit was weighty and his son He was heir apparent, neither obtained a proper end.
translations.idiomatic: Another interpretation holds that Quan trusted slanderers. Though Lu Xun's merit was great and his son He was crown prince, neither met a proper end.

sentences.zh: 與漢安帝聽讒、免楊震、廢太子同事也。

translations.literal: This was the same matter as Emperor An of Han listening to slander, dismissing Yang Zhen, and deposing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the case of Emperor An of Han, who heeded slander, dismissed Yang Zhen, and deposed the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 且赤烏中無年不用兵，百姓愁怨。

translations.literal: Moreover during Chiwu there was no year without warfare; the common people were full of grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, throughout the Chiwu era war was waged every year without exception, and the people groaned under grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，將軍馬茂等又圖逆雲。

translations.literal: In autumn of the eighth year, the general Ma Mao and others again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year, the general Ma Mao and others again plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年九月，淫雨過常，冀、兗、徐、豫四州水出，沒溺殺人，漂失財產。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, excessive rain beyond the norm; Ji, Yan, Xu, and Yu four provinces saw water rise, drowning and killing people and sweeping away property.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingchu, under Emperor Ming of Wei, rains fell far beyond the norm. In Ji, Yan, Xu, and Yu provinces the waters rose, drowning people and sweeping away property.

sentences.zh: 帝自初即位，便淫奢極欲，多占幼女，或奪士妻，崇飾宮室，妨害農戰，觸情恣欲，至是彌甚。

translations.literal: From the time he first took the throne the emperor was dissolute and extravagant to the utmost in desire, taking many young girls, sometimes seizing officers' wives, adorning palaces extravagantly, harming agriculture and warfare, indulging his passions at will—to this point it grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he took the throne the emperor gave himself to dissipation and extravagance, seizing many young girls and sometimes officers' wives, lavishing ornament on his palaces, and harming agriculture and military readiness as he indulged every whim—conduct that by this time had grown worse still.

sentences.zh: 號令逆時，饑不損役，此水不潤下之應也。

translations.literal: His commands went against the seasons; in famine he did not reduce corvée—this was the response to water not moistening downward.
translations.idiomatic: His edicts defied the seasons, and in famine he did not lighten corvée labor—this was the manifestation of water failing to flow downward.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳元年夏，大水。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Wufeng under Sun Liang of Wu, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Wufeng, under Sun Liang of Wu, a great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 亮即位四年，乃立權廟；

translations.literal: Four years after Liang took the throne he finally established Quan's temple;
translations.idiomatic: Only four years after Liang took the throne did he establish a temple to Sun Quan;

sentences.zh: 又終吳世，不上祖宗之號，不修嚴父之禮，昭穆之數有闕。

translations.literal: through the entire Wu era he never bestowed ancestral temple titles, never performed the rites to the revered father, and the sequence of zhao and mu was incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: and through the entire Wu dynasty he never bestowed ancestral temple titles, never performed the rites to the revered father, and the proper sequence of zhao and mu temples remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 亮及休、皓又並廢二郊，不秩群神。

translations.literal: Liang, Xiu, and Hao together also abolished the two suburban sacrifices and did not rank the host of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Xiu, and Hao alike abolished the two suburban sacrifices and offered no ranked worship to the host of spirits.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟，不祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for abbreviating the ancestral temples and not sacrificing.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for curtailing the ancestral temples and neglecting sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又是時，孫峻專政，陰勝陽之應乎。

translations.literal: Moreover at this time Sun Jun monopolized government—this was perhaps the response of yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Sun Jun monopolized power—perhaps another manifestation of yin overcoming yang.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休永安四年五月，大雨，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, great rain; springs and wells overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yong'an, under Sun Xiu of Wu, heavy rains fell and springs burst forth.

sentences.zh: 昔歲作浦裏塘，功費無數，而田不可成，士卒死叛，或自賊殺，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: The previous year they built the Puli embankment; labor and expense were countless yet the fields could not be completed; soldiers died or rebelled, some killing one another; the common people were full of grief and resentment—yin qi was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, work on the Puli embankment had consumed vast labor and expense yet the fields could not be brought into cultivation. Soldiers died or deserted; some turned bandit and killed one another. The people groaned with grief and resentment—yin had grown overpowering.

sentences.zh: 休又專任張布，退盛沖等，吳人賊之之應也。

translations.literal: Xiu also relied exclusively on Zhang Bu and pushed aside Sheng Chong and others—this was perhaps the response to Wu people becoming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu also placed sole trust in Zhang Bu while pushing aside Sheng Chong and others—perhaps the reason Wu turned to brigandage.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休永安五年八月壬午，大雨震電，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the fifth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, great rain, thunder and lightning; springs overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the fifth year of Yong'an, under Sun Xiu of Wu, torrential rain fell amid thunder and lightning, and springs burst forth.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始四年九月，青、徐、兗、豫四州大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu four provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taishi, under Emperor Wu of Jin, Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu provinces were struck by great floods.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，大雨霖，河、洛、伊、沁皆溢，殺二百餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, great rains poured in succession; the Yellow River, Luo, Yi, and Qin all overflowed, killing more than two hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year, torrential rains fell without cease. The Yellow River, Luo, Yi, and Qin all burst their banks and killed more than two hundred people.

sentences.zh: 帝即尊位，不加三後祖宗之號。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the honored position, he did not bestow ancestral temple titles on the three empresses.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, he did not bestow ancestral temple titles upon the three empresses.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，又除明堂南郊五帝坐，同稱昊天上帝，一位而已。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he also removed the seats of the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall and southern suburb, calling them all by the single title August Heaven Supreme Lord, one position only.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he also removed the seats of the Five Emperors at the Bright Hall and southern suburban altar, uniting them under the single title August Heaven Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 又省先後配地之禮。

translations.literal: He also reduced the rites of matching the former and later empresses to the earth altar.
translations.idiomatic: He further abolished the rites by which the former and later empresses were paired at the earth altar.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟，廢祭祀之罰，與漢成帝同事。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for abbreviating the ancestral temples and abolishing sacrifices—the same matter as Emperor Cheng of Han.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for curtailing the ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice—the same offense as under Emperor Cheng of Han.

sentences.zh: 一曰，昔歲及此年，藥蘭泥、白虎文秦涼殺刺史胡烈、牽弘，遣田璋討泥。

translations.literal: One view says: in the previous year and this year, Yaolan Ni and Baihu Wen of Liang and Liang killed the inspector Hu Lie and Qian Hong; Tian Zhang was sent to attack Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Another interpretation notes that in the previous year and this one, Yaolan Ni and Baihu Wen of Liang and Liang killed the inspector Hu Lie and Qian Hong, after which Tian Zhang was dispatched to attack Ni.

sentences.zh: 又司馬望以大眾次淮北禦孫皓。

translations.literal: Moreover Sima Wang with a great host encamped north of the Huai to resist Sun Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang also encamped north of the Huai with a great army to resist Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 內外兵役，西州饑亂，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Warfare at home and abroad; famine and disorder in the western provinces; the common people full of grief and resentment—yin qi was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: War raged at home and abroad; famine and rebellion gripped the western provinces; the people groaned with grief and resentment—yin had grown overpowering.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，始上祖宗號，太熙初，還複五帝位。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning he first bestowed ancestral temple titles; at the beginning of Taixi he restored the seats of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era he first bestowed ancestral temple titles; early in the Taixi era he restored the seats of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年六月，泰山、江夏大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, Mount Tai and Jiangxia suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, Mount Tai and Jiangxia were struck by great floods.

sentences.zh: 泰山流三百家，殺六千餘人；

translations.literal: At Mount Tai the current swept away three hundred households, killing more than six thousand people;
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Tai the flood carried off three hundred households and killed more than six thousand people;

sentences.zh: 江夏亦殺人。

translations.literal: Jiangxia also killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia also saw deaths.

sentences.zh: 是時平吳後，王浚為元功，而詆劾妄加；

translations.literal: At this time after the pacification of Wu, Wang Jun was the chief meritorious one, yet slander and impeachment were heaped on him without cause;
translations.idiomatic: At this time, after the conquest of Wu, Wang Jun had been the foremost contributor to victory, yet baseless slander and impeachment were heaped upon him;

sentences.zh: 荀、賈為無謀，而並蒙重賞。

translations.literal: Xun and Jia were without strategy yet both received heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: while Xun and Jia, though devoid of merit, both received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 收吳姬五千，納之後宮。

translations.literal: He took five thousand Wu concubines into the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: He took five thousand women of Wu into the harem.

sentences.zh: 此其應也。

translations.literal: This was its response.
translations.idiomatic: This was the corresponding manifestation.

sentences.zh: 太康四年七月，司、豫、徐、兗、荊、揚郡國二十大水，傷秋稼，壞屋室，有死者。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taikang, twenty commanderies and kingdoms of Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Jing, and Yang suffered great flood, harming the autumn crops, destroying houses, with some dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taikang, twenty commanderies and kingdoms across Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Jing, and Yang were flooded. Autumn crops were ruined, houses destroyed, and some people died.

sentences.zh: 太康六年三月，青、涼、幽、冀郡國十五大水。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, fifteen commanderies and kingdoms of Qing, Liang, You, and Ji suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, fifteen commanderies and kingdoms in Qing, Liang, You, and Ji were flooded.

sentences.zh: 太康七年九月，西方安定等郡國八大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Taikang, eight commanderies and kingdoms of the western region including Anding suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year of Taikang, eight western commanderies and kingdoms including Anding were flooded.

sentences.zh: 太康八年六月，郡國八大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taikang, eight commanderies and kingdoms suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taikang, eight commanderies and kingdoms were flooded.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康二年，有水災。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, there was a water disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuankang, under Emperor Hui of Jin, floods struck.

sentences.zh: 元康五年五月，潁川、淮南大水；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, Yingchuan and Huainan suffered great flood;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, Yingchuan and Huainan were flooded;

sentences.zh: 六月，城陽、東莞大水殺人；

translations.literal: in the sixth month, Chengyang and Dongguan great flood killed people;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month, floods in Chengyang and Dongguan killed people;

sentences.zh: 荊、揚、徐、兗、豫五州又大水。

translations.literal: Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, and Yu five provinces again suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: and Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, and Yu provinces were flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是時帝即位已五載，猶未郊祀，烝嘗亦多不身親近。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had been on the throne for five years yet still had not performed suburban sacrifice; the seasonal offerings were also often not attended by him in person.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the emperor had reigned five years yet still had not performed the suburban sacrifices, and he often did not attend the seasonal offerings in person.

sentences.zh: 簡宗廟，廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for abbreviating the ancestral temples and abolishing sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for curtailing the ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 班固曰：「王者即位，必郊祀天地，望秩山川。

translations.literal: Ban Gu says: "When a king takes the throne, he must sacrifice at the suburbs to Heaven and Earth and offer ranked worship to the mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu writes: "When a king takes the throne, he must sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars and offer ranked worship to the mountains and rivers."

sentences.zh: 若乃不敬鬼神，政令違逆，則霧水暴至，百川逆溢，壞鄉邑，溺人民，水不潤下也。

translations.literal: If one does not respect ghosts and spirits and government orders go against principle, then misty water arrives violently, the hundred streams overflow in reverse, destroying villages and towns and drowning the people—water not moistening downward.
translations.idiomatic: If he fails to honor the spirits, and his edicts defy right principle, then mist and flood descend violently, the hundred streams reverse their course, villages are destroyed, and people are drowned—water failing to flow downward.

sentences.zh: 」元康六年五月，荊、揚二州大水。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuankang, Jing and Yang two provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuankang, Jing and Yang provinces were flooded.

sentences.zh: 按董仲舒說，水者，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: According to Dong Zhongshu's doctrine, water is the flourishing of yin qi.
translations.idiomatic: According to Dong Zhongshu's doctrine, water signifies the dominance of yin.

sentences.zh: 是時賈後亂朝，寵樹賈、郭。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia threw the court into disorder, favoring and elevating the Jia and Guo clans.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Empress Jia threw the court into turmoil, elevating the Jia and Guo clans.

sentences.zh: 女主專政之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to a female ruler monopolizing government.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of a woman monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 元康八年五月，金墉城井水溢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuankang, the well water at Jincheng overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuankang, the well at Jincheng overflowed.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝時有此妖，班固以為王莽之象。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han there was this prodigy; Ban Gu took it as an image of Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: A similar prodigy had appeared under Emperor Cheng of Han, which Ban Gu interpreted as a portent of Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 及趙倫篡位，即此應也。

translations.literal: When Zhao Lun usurped the throne, this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Lun seized the throne, this was the corresponding manifestation.

sentences.zh: 倫廢帝於此城，井溢所在，又天意乎！

translations.literal: Lun deposed the emperor at this fortress; the place where the well overflowed—was this again Heaven's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Lun had deposed the emperor at this fortress—the very place where the well overflowed. Was this not Heaven's intent again!

sentences.zh: 元康八年九月，荊、揚、徐、兗、冀五州大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Yuankang, Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, and Ji five provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Yuankang, Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, and Ji provinces were flooded.

sentences.zh: 是時賈後暴戾滋甚，韓謐驕猜彌扇，卒害太子，旋亦禍滅。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia's violence and cruelty grew daily worse; Han Mi's arrogance and suspicion spread ever further; in the end they harmed the crown prince, and soon they too were destroyed by calamity.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Empress Jia's cruelty had grown extreme, and Han Mi's arrogance and suspicion ran rampant. In the end they destroyed the crown prince, and soon met their own ruin.

sentences.zh: 元康九年四月，宮中井水沸溢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, the palace well water boiled and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, the palace well boiled over.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉四年四月，江東大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, the lands east of the Yangtze suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, under Emperor Huai of Jin, the lands east of the Yangtze were flooded.

sentences.zh: 是時，王導等潛懷翼戴之計。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dao and others secretly harbored plans to support and elevate a new ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Dao and others were secretly laying plans to support a new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Yin qi was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had grown overpowering.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興三年六月，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Taixing, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, a great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦內懷不臣，傲很作威，後終夷滅。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun harbored disloyalty within, acting arrogant and fierce to display his power; in the end he was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Dun harbored treasonous intent, ruling with arrogance and brutality until he was finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 大興四年七月，大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Daxing, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Daxing, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 明年有石頭之敗。

translations.literal: The following year there was the defeat at Stone Castle.
translations.idiomatic: The following year came the defeat at Stone Castle.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌二年五月，荊州及丹陽、宣城、吳興、壽春大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, Jing Province and Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, and Shouchun suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Yongchang, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Jing Province and Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, and Shouchun were flooded.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和四年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yonghe, under Emperor Mu of Jin, a great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時幼主沖弱，母后臨朝；

translations.literal: At this time the young ruler was weak and immature, and the empress dowager held court;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the young emperor was still a child, and the empress dowager held the reins of government;

sentences.zh: 又將相大臣，各爭權政。

translations.literal: moreover the generals, ministers, and great officials each contended for power in government.
translations.idiomatic: while generals, ministers, and great officials wrestled among themselves for power.

sentences.zh: 與咸和初同事也。

translations.literal: This was the same matter as at the beginning of Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the situation at the beginning of the Xianhe era.

sentences.zh: 永和五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghe, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghe, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 永和六年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yonghe, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yonghe, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 永和七年七月甲辰夜，濤水入石頭，死者數百人。

translations.literal: On the night of the jiachen day of the seventh month of the seventh year of Yonghe, tidal water entered Stone Castle, and several hundred people died.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the jiachen day in the seventh month of the seventh year of Yonghe, tidal water surged into Stone Castle and killed several hundred people.

sentences.zh: 去年，殷浩以私忿廢蔡謨，遐邇非之。

translations.literal: In the previous year Yin Hao dismissed Cai Mo out of private resentment; near and far condemned it.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Yin Hao had dismissed Cai Mo out of personal spite, drawing condemnation from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 又幼主在上，而殷、桓交惡，選徒聚甲，各崇私權。

translations.literal: Moreover with the young ruler above, Yin and Huan were mutually hostile, selecting troops and gathering armor, each exalting private power.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with a child on the throne, Yin Hao and Huan Wen were locked in enmity, each raising troops and amassing arms to advance his private power.

sentences.zh: 陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: This was a manifestation of yin overcoming yang.

sentences.zh: 一說濤入石頭，江右以為兵占。

translations.literal: One view says that when the tide entered Stone Castle, the lands south of the Yangtze took it as a military omen.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that when the tide entered Stone Castle, the lands south of the Yangtze read it as a portent of war.

sentences.zh: 是後殷浩、桓溫、謝尚、荀羨連年征伐。

translations.literal: After this Yin Hao, Huan Wen, Xie Shang, and Xun Xian waged campaigns year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yin Hao, Huan Wen, Xie Shang, and Xun Xian campaigned year after year without cease.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平二年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Shengping, under Emperor Mu of Jin, a great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫權制朝廷，征伐是專。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen controlled the court by power and monopolized military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Huan Wen dominated the court and monopolized every campaign.

sentences.zh: 升平五年四月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Shengping, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Shengping, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 晉海西太和六年六月，京都大水，平地數尺，侵及太廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taihe of the Deposed Emperor of Jin, the capital suffered great flood; on level ground the water stood several feet deep and reached the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taihe, under the Deposed Emperor of Jin, the capital was flooded. Water stood several feet deep on level ground and reached the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 硃雀大航纜斷，三艘流入大江。

translations.literal: The cables of the Vermilion Bird great bridge broke, and three vessels drifted into the great river.
translations.idiomatic: The mooring cables of the Vermilion Bird bridge snapped, and three vessels were swept into the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 丹陽、晉陵、吳國、吳興、臨海五郡又大水，稻稼蕩沒，黎庶饑饉。

translations.literal: Danyang, Jinling, Wu Kingdom, Wuxing, and Linhai five commanderies again suffered great flood; rice crops were swept away, and the common people suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang, Jinling, Wu, Wuxing, and Linhai were flooded again. Crops were destroyed, and the people faced famine.

sentences.zh: 初四年，桓溫北伐敗績，十喪其九；

translations.literal: Earlier in the fourth year Huan Wen's northern campaign met defeat; nine out of ten were lost;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Huan Wen's northern campaign had ended in disaster, with nine men in ten lost;

sentences.zh: 五年，又征淮南，逾歲乃克。

translations.literal: in the fifth year he again campaigned against Huainan, and only after more than a year did he conquer.
translations.idiomatic: in the fifth year he campaigned against Huainan again, and only after more than a year did he prevail.

sentences.zh: 百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to the common people's grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of popular grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元三年六月，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Taixuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Taixuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時孝武幼弱，政在將相。

translations.literal: At this time Xiaowu was young and weak; government lay with the generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Xiaowu was still a child, and power rested with the generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 太元五年，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taixuan, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taixuan, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 去年氐賊攻沒襄陽，又向廣陵。

translations.literal: In the previous year the Di bandits attacked and overran Xiangyang and also advanced toward Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Di forces had overrun Xiangyang and advanced toward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 於是逼徙江、淮民悉令南渡，三州失業，道饉相望。

translations.literal: Thereupon they compelled the people of the Jiang and Huai regions to cross south en masse; the three provinces lost their livelihoods, and starvation lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The court then forced the people of the Jiang and Huai regions to flee south en masse. Three provinces were stripped of their livelihoods, and the roads were lined with the starving.

sentences.zh: 謝玄雖破句難等，自後征戍不已。

translations.literal: Though Xie Xuan defeated Gou Nan and others, from then on campaigns and garrisons never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xie Xuan had defeated Gou Nan and his allies, campaigns and garrison duty never ceased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to the common people's grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of popular grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 太元六年六月，荊、江揚三州大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taixuan, Jing, Jiang, and Yang three provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taixuan, Jing, Jiang, and Yang provinces were flooded.

sentences.zh: 太元十年夏，大水。

translations.literal: In summer of the tenth year of Taixuan, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the tenth year of Taixuan, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 初八年，破苻堅，自後有事中州，役無已歲。

translations.literal: Earlier in the eighth year they defeated Fu Jian; from then on there were affairs in the central provinces, and corvée never ceased year after year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they had defeated Fu Jian, but thereafter campaigns in the central provinces continued, and corvée labor never ceased from one year to the next.

sentences.zh: 兵民愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to soldiers and common people full of grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of grief and resentment among soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 太元十三年十二月，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Taixuan, tidal water entered Stone Castle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Taixuan, tidal water surged into Stone Castle.

sentences.zh: 明年，丁零、鮮卑寇擾司、兗鎮戍，西、北疲於奔命。

translations.literal: The following year the Dingling and Xianbei raided and harassed the garrisons of Si and Yan; west and north were exhausted from rushing to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Dingling and Xianbei raiders harassed the garrisons of Si and Yan, and the western and northern frontiers were worn out by constant emergency marches.

sentences.zh: 太元十五年七月，兗州大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Taixuan, Yan Province suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Taixuan, Yan Province was flooded.

sentences.zh: 是時緣河紛爭，征戍勤悴。

translations.literal: At this time strife along the river banks was unceasing; campaigns and garrisons wore men down with toil.
translations.idiomatic: At this time fighting along the Yellow River never ceased, and campaigns and garrisons exhausted every man.

sentences.zh: 太元十七年六月甲寅，濤水入石頭，毀大航，漂船舫，有死者；

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Taixuan, tidal water entered Stone Castle, destroyed the great bridge, swept away boats, and some died;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Taixuan, tidal water surged into Stone Castle, destroyed the great bridge, swept away boats, and killed some people;

sentences.zh: 京口西浦，亦濤入殺人。

translations.literal: at the western ford of Jingkou the tide also entered and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: at the western ford of Jingkou the tide also surged in and killed people.

sentences.zh: 永嘉郡潮水湧起，近海四縣人民多死。

translations.literal: In Yongjia Commandery the tide surged up, and in four coastal counties many people died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia Commandery the tide surged, and in four coastal counties many people died.

sentences.zh: 後四年帝崩，而王恭再攻京師。

translations.literal: Four years later the emperor died, and Wang Gong again attacked the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the emperor died, and Wang Gong attacked the capital again.

sentences.zh: 京師亦發大眾以禦之。

translations.literal: The capital also raised a great host to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The capital in turn raised a great army to resist him.

sentences.zh: 太元十九年七月，荊州、彭城大水傷稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year of Taixuan, Jing Province and Pengcheng suffered great flood harming the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year of Taixuan, floods in Jing Province and Pengcheng ruined the crops.

sentences.zh: 太元二十年，荊州、彭城大水。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taixuan, Jing Province and Pengcheng suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Taixuan, Jing Province and Pengcheng were flooded again.

sentences.zh: 太元二十一年五月癸卯，大水。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the twenty-first year of Taixuan, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the twenty-first year of Taixuan, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時政事多弊，兆庶非之。

translations.literal: At this time government affairs had many abuses, and the myriad people condemned them.
translations.idiomatic: At this time government was rife with abuses, and the people condemned it on all sides.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安三年五月，荊州大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, Jing Province suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Long'an, under Emperor An of Jin, Jing Province was flooded.

sentences.zh: 去年，殷仲堪舉兵向京都；

translations.literal: In the previous year Yin Zhongkan raised troops toward the capital;
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Yin Zhongkan had raised troops against the capital;

sentences.zh: 是年春，又殺郗恢。

translations.literal: that spring he also killed Chi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: and that spring he also killed Chi Hui.

sentences.zh: 陰盛作威之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to flourishing yin displaying its power.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of overpowering yin asserting its dominance.

sentences.zh: 仲堪尋亦敗亡。

translations.literal: Zhongkan soon also met defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan soon met defeat and ruin as well.

sentences.zh: 隆安五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Long'an, great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Long'an, another great flood struck.

sentences.zh: 是時司馬元顯作威陵上，又桓玄擅西夏，孫恩亂東國。

translations.literal: At this time Sima Yuanxian displayed his power and overawed his superiors; moreover Huan Xuan monopolized the western Xia region, and Sun En threw the eastern states into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Sima Yuanxian lorded it over his superiors, Huan Xuan seized control of the western regions, and Sun En threw the eastern provinces into chaos.

sentences.zh: 陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: This was another manifestation of yin overcoming yang.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興二年十二月，桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, Huan Xuan usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 其明年二月庚寅夜，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: On the night of the gengyin day of the second month of the following year, tidal water entered Stone Castle.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the gengyin day in the second month of the following year, tidal water surged into Stone Castle.

sentences.zh: 是時貢使商旅，方舟萬計，漂敗流斷，骸胔相望。

translations.literal: At this time tribute envoys and traveling merchants numbered tens of thousands of boats in convoy; they were swept away and broken, drifting in fragments, corpses in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: At this time tribute missions and merchant fleets numbered in the tens of thousands of vessels. They were smashed and swept away in fragments, corpses lining the waters as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 江右雖有濤變，未有若斯之甚。

translations.literal: Though the lands south of the Yangtze had seen tidal changes, none had been as severe as this.
translations.idiomatic: The lands south of the Yangtze had seen tidal disasters before, but never one so devastating.

sentences.zh: 三月，義軍克京都，玄敗走，遂夷滅。

translations.literal: In the third month the righteous army took the capital; Xuan fled in defeat and was finally exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the loyalist army took the capital. Xuan fled in defeat and was finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 元興三年二月己醜朔夜，濤水入石頭，漂沒殺人，大航流敗。

translations.literal: On the night of the first day of the second month, the jichou day of the third year of Yuanxing, tidal water entered Stone Castle, sweeping away and drowning people; the great bridge was carried off in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the new moon, the jichou day of the second month of the third year of Yuanxing, tidal water surged into Stone Castle, drowning people and sweeping everything away. The great bridge was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉五年六月，京邑大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the capital region suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia, under Emperor Wen of Song, the capital region was flooded.

sentences.zh: 七年，右將軍到彥之率師入河。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the General of the Right Dao Yanzhi led an army into the Yellow River region.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the General of the Right Dao Yanzhi led his army into the Yellow River region.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年五月，京邑大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Yuanjia, the capital region suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Yuanjia, the capital region was flooded again.

sentences.zh: 十三年，司空檀道濟誅。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Minister of Works Tan Daoji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Minister of Works Tan Daoji was put to death.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年六月，丹陽、淮南、吳、吳興、義興五郡大水，京邑乘船。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yuanjia, Danyang, Huainan, Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing five commanderies suffered great flood; in the capital one traveled by boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yuanjia, Danyang, Huainan, Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing were flooded, and in the capital people traveled by boat.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年五月，江水泛溢，沒居民，害苗稼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, the Yangtze overflowed, drowning residents and harming the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, the Yangtze overflowed, drowning residents and destroying the crops.

sentences.zh: 明年，右軍將軍裴方明率雍、梁之眾伐仇池。

translations.literal: The following year the General of the Right Army Pei Fangming led the hosts of Yong and Liang to attack Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the General of the Right Army Pei Fangming led the armies of Yong and Liang against Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年、二十年，東諸郡大水。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth and twentieth years of Yuanjia, the eastern commanderies suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth and twentieth years of Yuanjia, the eastern commanderies were flooded.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年五月，京邑大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, the capital region suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, the capital region was flooded again.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建元年八月，會稽大水，平地八尺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, Kuaiji suffered great flood; on level ground the water stood eight feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Xiaojian, under Emperor Xiaowu, Kuaiji was flooded. On level ground the water stood eight feet deep.

sentences.zh: 後二年，虜寇青、冀州，遣羽林軍卒討伐。

translations.literal: Two years later the barbarians raided Qing and Ji provinces, and imperial guardsmen were dispatched to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later northern enemies raided Qing and Ji provinces, and imperial guardsmen were sent to repel them.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明元年五月，吳興、義興大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, Wuxing and Yixing suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Daming, under Emperor Xiaowu, Wuxing and Yixing were flooded.

sentences.zh: 大明四年八月，雍州大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Daming, Yong Province suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Daming, Yong Province was flooded.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，南徐、南兗州大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, southern Xu and southern Yan provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, southern Xu and southern Yan provinces were flooded.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年六月，壽陽大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor, Shouchun suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Yuanhui, under the Deposed Emperor, Shouchun was flooded.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明元年七月，雍州大水，甚于關羽樊城時。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Shengming of Emperor Shun, Yong Province suffered great flood, more severe than at the time of Guan Yu at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Shengming, under Emperor Shun, Yong Province was flooded more severely than at Guan Yu's siege of Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 升明二年二月，於潛翼異山一夕五十二處水出，流漂居民。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shengming, at Mount Yiyi in Yuqian, in one night water burst forth at fifty-two places, sweeping away residents in the current.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Shengming, at Mount Yiyi in Yuqian, water burst from fifty-two places in a single night and swept residents away.

sentences.zh: 七月丙午朔，濤水入石頭，居民皆漂沒。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, the bingwu day, tidal water entered Stone Castle, and all residents were swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon, the bingwu day of the seventh month, tidal water surged into Stone Castle and drowned the inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 恆寒：

translations.literal: Constant cold:
translations.idiomatic: Constant cold:

sentences.zh: 庶征之恆寒，劉歆以為「大雨雪、及未當雨雪而雨雪、及大雨雹、隕霜殺菽草，皆常寒之罰也」。

translations.literal: Among the various signs, constant cold—Liu Xin held that "great rain and snow, rain and snow when it should not yet rain and snow, great hail, and falling frost killing beans and grasses are all punishments of constant cold."
translations.idiomatic: Among the various omens, constant cold—Liu Xin held that "heavy rain and snow, rain and snow out of season, great hail, and frost that kills beans and grasses are all manifestations of constant cold as punishment."

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「有德遭險，茲謂逆命。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "The virtuous meeting danger—this is called defying fate."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When the virtuous meet danger, that is called defying Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 厥異寒。

translations.literal: Its anomaly is cold.
translations.idiomatic: The anomaly is cold.

sentences.zh: 誅罰過深，當燠而寒，盡六日，亦為雹。

translations.literal: Punishments too deep—when it should be warm yet is cold, for six full days, this also becomes hail.
translations.idiomatic: When punishments run too deep, warmth turns to cold for six full days, and hail may follow.

sentences.zh: 害正不誅，茲謂養賊。

translations.literal: Harming the upright yet not punishing—this is called nurturing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Harming the upright without punishing the guilty—this is called nurturing bandits.

sentences.zh: 寒七十二日，殺飛禽。

translations.literal: Cold for seventy-two days kills flying birds.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two days of cold will kill the birds.

sentences.zh: 道人始去，茲謂傷。

translations.literal: When the Way-person first departs—this is called injury.
translations.idiomatic: When men of the Way are first driven away, that is called injury.

sentences.zh: 其寒物無霜而死，湧水出。

translations.literal: Its cold: things die without frost; surging water appears.
translations.idiomatic: Its cold kills living things without frost, and surging waters appear.

sentences.zh: 戰不量敵，茲謂辱命。

translations.literal: Fighting without measuring the enemy—this is called disgracing one's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Going to war without gauging the enemy—this is called disgracing one's mandate.

sentences.zh: 其寒雖雨物不茂。」

translations.literal: Its cold: though it rains, things do not flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Its cold: though rain falls, nothing thrives."

sentences.zh: 吳孫權嘉禾三年九月朔，隕霜傷穀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month of the third year of Jiahe under Sun Quan of Wu, falling frost harmed the grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month of the third year of Jiahe, under Sun Quan of Wu, frost fell and damaged the grain.

sentences.zh: 按劉向說：「誅罰不由君出，在臣下之象也」。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's doctrine: "When punishments do not issue from the ruler, this is an image of power residing in subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's doctrine: "When punishments do not issue from the ruler, power has passed to his subordinates."

sentences.zh: 是時校事呂壹專作威福，與漢元帝時石顯用事隕霜同應。

translations.literal: At this time the investigator Lü Yi monopolized power and favor; this matched the response of falling frost when Shi Xian held power under Emperor Yuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the investigator Lü Yi monopolized power and favor—the same manifestation as the frost that fell when Shi Xian dominated the court under Emperor Yuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 班固書九月二日，陳壽言朔，皆明未可以傷穀也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu records the second day of the ninth month; Chen Shou says the first day—both make clear that the grain could not yet have been harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu dates it to the second day of the ninth month, while Chen Shou says the first day—both making clear that the grain could not yet have been ripe enough to suffer damage.

sentences.zh: 壹後亦伏誅。

translations.literal: Yi was later also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was later executed as well.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「興兵妄誅，茲謂亡法。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "Raising troops and punishing rashly—this is called the loss of law."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "Raising troops and punishing without cause—this is called the abandonment of law."

sentences.zh: 厥災霜，夏殺五穀，冬殺麥。

translations.literal: Its calamity is frost; in summer it kills the five grains, in winter it kills wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity is frost: in summer it destroys the five grains, in winter it destroys the wheat.

sentences.zh: 誅不原情，茲謂不仁。

translations.literal: Punishing without tracing the facts—this is called lack of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing without investigating the facts—this is called want of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 其霜夏先大雷風，冬先雨，乃隕霜，有芒角。

translations.literal: Its frost: in summer great thunder and wind come first; in winter rain comes first; then frost falls, with pointed rays.
translations.idiomatic: Its frost: in summer comes first great thunder and wind; in winter comes first rain; then frost falls, sharp-pointed.

sentences.zh: 賢聖遭害，其霜附木不下地。

translations.literal: When the worthy and sage suffer harm, its frost clings to trees and does not reach the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When the worthy and sage suffer harm, the frost clings to the trees and never reaches the ground.

sentences.zh: 佞人依刑，茲謂私賊。

translations.literal: When flatterers rely on punishments, this is called a private thief.
translations.idiomatic: When sycophants lean on the penal code, that is called covert brigandage.

sentences.zh: 其霜在草根土隙間。

translations.literal: Its frost is among grass roots and in crevices in the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Its frost settles among grass roots and in the cracks of the earth.

sentences.zh: 不教而誅，茲謂虐。

translations.literal: Punishing without instructing first—this is called cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: To punish without teaching first—that is called tyranny.

sentences.zh: 其霜反在草下。」

translations.literal: Its frost is instead beneath the grass."
translations.idiomatic: Its frost lies beneath the grass instead."

sentences.zh: 嘉禾四年七月，雨雹，又隕霜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Jiahe, hail fell, and falling frost appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Jiahe, hail fell, and frost fell again.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說：「雹者陰脅陽」。

translations.literal: Examining Liu Xiang's explanation: "Hail is yin coercing yang."
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's account: "Hail is yin coercing yang."

sentences.zh: 是時呂壹作威用事，詆毀重臣，排陷無辜。

translations.literal: At this time Lü Yi wielded power arrogantly, slandered great ministers, and framed the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Lü Yi lorded it over the court, defamed senior officials, and framed innocent men.

sentences.zh: 自太子登以下，鹹患毒之，而壹反獲封侯寵異。

translations.literal: From Crown Prince Deng downward, all alike suffered his poison, yet Yi in turn received enfeoffment as marquis and extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: From Crown Prince Deng on down, everyone alike suffered under his venom, yet Yi was enfeoffed as a marquis and showered with special favor.

sentences.zh: 與《春秋》公子遂專任，雨雹同應也。

translations.literal: This matched the hail that responded when Gongsun Sui held sole power in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: This was the same hail-borne response as when Gongsun Sui monopolized power in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝信讒，多殺無辜，亦雨雹。

translations.literal: Emperor An of Han believed slander, killed many innocents, and hail also fell.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An of Han heeded slander, put many innocent men to death, and hail fell as well.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒曰「凡雹皆為有所脅，行專一之政」故也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu said, "Whenever hail occurs, something is being coerced; it comes from carrying out monopolized government"—for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu said that "all hail arises when something is coerced—it comes from rule exercised by a single hand alone."

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏四年正月，大雪，平地深三尺，鳥獸死者太半。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chiwu, under Sun Quan of Wu, great snow fell; on level ground it was three chi deep, and more than half the birds and beasts died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Chiwu, under Sun Quan of Wu, heavy snow fell until the level ground lay three chi deep, and more than half the birds and beasts perished.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，全琮等四將軍攻略淮南、襄陽，戰死者千餘人。

translations.literal: That summer, the four generals including Quan Cong attacked Huainan and Xiangyang; more than a thousand died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, four generals led by Quan Cong campaigned against Huainan and Xiangyang, and more than a thousand men fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 其後權以讒邪，數責讓陸議，議憤恚致卒。

translations.literal: Afterwards Quan, believing slander, repeatedly rebuked Lu Yi, and Yi died of rage and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Quan, swayed by slander, rebuked Lu Yi again and again until Yi died of fury and indignation.

sentences.zh: 與漢景、武大雪同事也。

translations.literal: This was the same matter as the great snow under Emperors Jing and Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the great snows under Emperors Jing and Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 赤烏十一年四月，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year of Chiwu, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year of Chiwu, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是時權聽讒，將危太子。

translations.literal: At this time Quan listened to slander and was about to endanger the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Quan heeded slander and was on the verge of putting the crown prince in peril.

sentences.zh: 其後硃據、屈晃以迕意黜辱，陳象以忠諫族誅，而太子終廢。

translations.literal: Afterwards Zhu Ju and Qu Huang were disgraced and dismissed for displeasing him; Chen Xiang was executed along with his clan for loyal remonstrance, and in the end the crown prince was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Ju and Qu Huang were humiliated and removed for crossing him; Chen Xiang was executed to the last of his clan for loyal remonstrance, and the crown prince was finally deposed.

sentences.zh: 此有德遭險，誅罰過深之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response when the virtuous met danger and punishments ran too deep.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of the virtuous meeting peril and punishments carried too far.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始六年冬，大雪。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Taishi, under Emperor Wu of Jin, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year of Taishi, under Emperor Wu of Jin, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年十二月，大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Taishi, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Taishi, heavy snow fell again.

sentences.zh: 明年。

translations.literal: The following year.
translations.idiomatic: The following year,

sentences.zh: 有步闡、楊肇之敗，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: There were the defeats of Bu Chan and Yang Zhao; the dead and wounded were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: came the defeats of Bu Chan and Yang Zhao, with casualties numbering in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年四月辛未，隕霜。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the fourth month of the ninth year of Taishi, falling frost appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the fourth month of the ninth year of Taishi, frost fell.

sentences.zh: 是時賈充親党比周用事。

translations.literal: At this time Jia Chong's clique and partisans banded together and held power.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jia Chong's kin and allies formed factions and dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 與魯定公、漢元帝時隕霜同應也。

translations.literal: This matched the falling frost under Duke Ding of Lu and Emperor Yuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: This was the same falling-frost response as under Duke Ding of Lu and Emperor Yuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧三年八月，平原、安平、上党、秦郡霜害三豆。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, under Emperor Wu of Jin, frost in Pingyuan, Anping, Shangdang, and Qin commanderies harmed the three legumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, under Emperor Wu of Jin, frost in Pingyuan, Anping, Shangdang, and Qin commanderies damaged soybeans, small beans, and other legumes.

sentences.zh: 咸寧三年八月，河間暴風寒冰，郡國五隕霜傷穀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, violent winds and icy cold struck Hejian; five commanderies and kingdoms saw falling frost that harmed grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, violent winds and freezing cold struck Hejian, and falling frost in five commanderies and kingdoms damaged the grain.

sentences.zh: 是後大舉征吳，馬隆又帥精勇討涼州。

translations.literal: Afterwards he launched a major campaign against Wu, and Ma Long also led elite troops to suppress Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards a great campaign was launched against Wu, and Ma Long also led crack troops to pacify Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸甯五年五月丁亥，钜鹿、魏郡雨雹傷禾、麥；

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Xianning, hail in Julu and Wei commanderies harmed millet and wheat;
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Xianning, hail in Julu and Wei commanderies damaged millet and wheat;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，雁門雨雹傷秋稼＃咸寧五年六月庚戌，汲郡、廣平、陳留、滎陽雨雹；

translations.literal: On the xinmao day, hail in Yanmen harmed the autumn grain crops; on the gengxu day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Xianning, hail fell in Ji, Guangping, Chenliu, and Xingyang commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day, hail in Yanmen damaged the autumn crops; on the gengxu day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Xianning, hail fell in Ji, Guangping, Chenliu, and Xingyang commanderies;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，又雨雹，損傷秋麥千三百餘頃，壞屋百三十餘間；

translations.literal: On the bingchen day, hail fell again, damaging more than thirteen hundred qing of autumn wheat and destroying more than one hundred thirty houses;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, hail fell again, ruining more than thirteen hundred qing of autumn wheat and wrecking more than one hundred thirty dwellings;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，安定雨雹；

translations.literal: On the guihai day, hail fell in Anding;
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, hail fell in Anding;

sentences.zh: 七月丙申，魏郡又雨雹；

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, hail fell again in Wei commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, hail fell again in Wei commandery;

sentences.zh: 閏月壬子，新興又雨雹；

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the intercalary month, hail fell again in Xinxing;
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the intercalary month, hail fell again in Xinxing;

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，河東、弘農又雨雹，兼傷秋稼三豆。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the eighth month, hail fell again in Hedong and Hongnong, also harming autumn grain and the three legumes.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the eighth month, hail fell again in Hedong and Hongnong, damaging autumn crops and the three legumes as well.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年三月，河東、高平霜雹，傷桑、麥；

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, frost and hail in Hedong and Gaoping harmed mulberry and wheat;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, frost and hail in Hedong and Gaoping damaged mulberry and wheat;

sentences.zh: 四月，河南、河內、河東、魏郡、弘農雨雹，傷麥、豆；

translations.literal: In the fourth month, hail in Henan, Henei, Hedong, Wei commandery, and Hongnong harmed wheat and beans;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, hail in Henan, Henei, Hedong, Wei commandery, and Hongnong damaged wheat and beans;

sentences.zh: 五月，東平、平陽、上黨、雁門、濟南雨雹，傷禾、麥、三豆。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, hail in Dongping, Pingyang, Shangdang, Yanmen, and Jinan harmed millet, wheat, and the three legumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, hail in Dongping, Pingyang, Shangdang, Yanmen, and Jinan damaged millet, wheat, and the three legumes.

sentences.zh: 太康元年四月庚午，畿內縣二及東平范陽縣雨雹；

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the fourth month of the first year of Taikang, hail fell in two counties within the capital region and in Fanyang County of Dongping;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the fourth month of the first year of Taikang, hail fell in two counties of the capital region and in Fanyang County of Dongping;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，畿內縣五又雨雹。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day, hail fell again in five counties within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, hail fell again in five counties of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 是時王浚有大功，而權戚互加陷抑，帝從容不斷。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Jun had achieved great merit, yet powerful kinsmen repeatedly slandered and suppressed him, while the emperor remained unhurried and indecisive.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Jun had won great distinction, yet powerful relatives heaped slander and obstruction upon him while the emperor remained leisurely and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 陰脅陽之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of yin coercing yang.
translations.idiomatic: This was a manifestation of yin coercing yang.

sentences.zh: 太康二年二月辛酉，殞霜於濟南、琅邪，傷麥；

translations.literal: On the xinyou day of the second month of the second year of Taikang, falling frost in Jinan and Langya harmed wheat;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the second month of the second year of Taikang, falling frost in Jinan and Langya damaged wheat;

sentences.zh: 壬申，琅邪雨雪傷麥；

translations.literal: On the renshen day, rain and snow in Langya harmed wheat;
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, rain and snow in Langya damaged wheat;

sentences.zh: 三月甲午，河東隕霜害桑。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the third month, falling frost in Hedong harmed mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the third month, falling frost in Hedong damaged the mulberry.

sentences.zh: 太康二年五月丙戌，城陽、章武、琅邪傷麥；

translations.literal: On the bingxu day of the fifth month of the second year of Taikang, wheat was harmed in Chengyang, Zhangwu, and Langya;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day of the fifth month of the second year of Taikang, wheat was damaged in Chengyang, Zhangwu, and Langya;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，河東、樂安、東平、濟陰、弘農、濮陽、齊國、頓丘、魏郡、河內、汲郡、上黨雨雹，傷禾稼。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day, hail in Hedong, Le'an, Dongping, Jiyin, Hongnong, Puyang, Qi kingdom, Dunqiu, Wei commandery, Henei, Ji commandery, and Shangdang harmed grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, hail in Hedong, Le'an, Dongping, Jiyin, Hongnong, Puyang, Qi, Dunqiu, Wei commandery, Henei, Ji commandery, and Shangdang damaged the grain.

sentences.zh: 太康二年六月，郡國十六雨雹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang, hail fell in sixteen commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang, sixteen commanderies and kingdoms were struck by hail.

sentences.zh: 太康三年十二月，大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Taikang, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Taikang, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 太康五年七月乙卯，中山、東平雨雹，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, hail in Zhongshan and Dongping harmed the autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, hail in Zhongshan and Dongping damaged the autumn crops.

sentences.zh: 太康五年七月甲辰，中山雨雹；

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, hail fell in Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, hail fell in Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 九月，南安大雪折木。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, great snow in Nan'an snapped trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, heavy snow in Nan'an broke trees.

sentences.zh: 太康六年二月，東海霜傷桑、麥。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Taikang, frost in Donghai harmed mulberry and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Taikang, frost in Donghai damaged mulberry and wheat.

sentences.zh: 太康六年三月戊辰，齊郡臨菑、長廣不其等四縣，樂安梁鄒等八縣，琅邪臨沂等八縣，河間易城等六縣，高陽北新城等四縣，隕霜傷桑、麥。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, falling frost in four counties including Linzi of Qi commandery and Buqi of Changguang, eight counties including Liangzou of Le'an, eight counties including Linyi of Langya, six counties including Yicheng of Hejian, and four counties including Beixincheng of Gaoyang harmed mulberry and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, falling frost in four counties including Linzi of Qi and Buqi of Changguang, eight counties including Liangzou of Le'an, eight including Linyi of Langya, six including Yicheng of Hejian, and four including Beixincheng of Gaoyang damaged mulberry and wheat.

sentences.zh: 太康六年六月，滎陽、汲郡、雁門雨雹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taikang, hail fell in Xingyang, Ji commandery, and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taikang, hail fell in Xingyang, Ji commandery, and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 太康八年四月，齊國、天水二郡隕霜；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang, falling frost in Qi kingdom and Tianshui commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang, falling frost in Qi and Tianshui commanderies;

sentences.zh: 十二月，大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 太康九年正月，京都大風雨雹，髮屋拔木；

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Taikang, great wind and hail in the capital tore off roofs and uprooted trees;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Taikang, fierce wind and hail in the capital stripped roofs and uprooted trees;

sentences.zh: 四月，隴西隕霜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, falling frost in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, frost fell in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 太康十年四月，郡國八隕霜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taikang, falling frost in eight commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taikang, frost fell in eight commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康二年八月，沛及湯陰雨雹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yuankang, under Emperor Hui of Jin, hail fell in Pei and Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Yuankang, under Emperor Hui of Jin, hail fell in Pei and Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 元康三年四月，滎陽雨雹；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuankang, hail fell in Xingyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuankang, hail fell in Xingyang;

sentences.zh: 弘農湖、華陰又雨雹，深三尺。

translations.literal: Hail fell again in Hongnong Lake and Huayin, three chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hail fell again at Hongnong Lake and Huayin, piled three chi deep.

sentences.zh: 是時賈後凶淫專恣，與《春秋》魯桓夫人同事。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia was cruel, lewd, and willful—the same matter as Lady Wen of Duke Huan of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Empress Jia was cruel, licentious, and autocratic—the same case as the wife of Duke Huan of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: Yin was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was in the ascendant.

sentences.zh: 元康五年六月，東海雨雹，深五寸；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, hail in Donghai was five cun deep;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, hail in Donghai lay five cun deep;

sentences.zh: 十二月，丹陽雨雹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, hail fell in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, hail fell in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 元康五年十二月，丹陽建業大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, great snow fell in Jianye, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, heavy snow fell in Jianye, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 元康六年三月，東海隕霜殺桑、麥。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Yuankang, falling frost in Donghai killed mulberry and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Yuankang, falling frost in Donghai destroyed mulberry and wheat.

sentences.zh: 元康七年五月，魯國雨雹；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Yuankang, hail fell in Lu kingdom;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Yuankang, hail fell in Lu;

sentences.zh: 七月，秦、雍二州隕霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, falling frost in Qin and Yong provinces killed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, falling frost in Qin and Yong provinces destroyed the harvest.

sentences.zh: 元康九年三月旬有八日，河南、滎陽、潁川隕霜傷禾；

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the third month of the ninth year of Yuankang, falling frost in Henan, Xingyang, and Yingchuan harmed millet;
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the third month of the ninth year of Yuankang, falling frost in Henan, Xingyang, and Yingchuan damaged the grain;

sentences.zh: 五月，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是時賈後凶躁滋甚，是冬遂廢湣懷。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia's cruelty and recklessness grew ever worse; that winter she deposed Crown Prince Minhuai.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Empress Jia's cruelty and frenzy grew ever worse, and that winter she deposed Crown Prince Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興二年三月丁未，成都風雹殺人。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the third month of the second year of Taixing, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, wind and hail in Chengdu killed people.
