translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the third month of the second year of Taixing, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, wind and hail in Chengdu killed people.

sentences.zh: 太興三年三月，海鹽郡雨雹。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Taixing, hail fell in Haiyan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Taixing, hail fell in Haiyan commandery.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦陵上。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun was encroaching on the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Dun was encroaching upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌二年十二月，幽、冀、並三州大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yongchang, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, great snow fell in You, Ji, and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yongchang, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, heavy snow fell in You, Ji, and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝鹹和六年三月癸未，雨雹。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day of the third month of the sixth year of Xianhe, under Emperor Cheng of Jin, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the third month of the sixth year of Xianhe, under Emperor Cheng of Jin, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼弱，政在大臣。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was young and weak; government lay in the hands of the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was still a child, and power rested with the great ministers.

sentences.zh: 咸和九年八月，成都雪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Xianhe, snow fell in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Xianhe, snow fell in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 其日李雄死。

translations.literal: That day Li Xiong died.
translations.idiomatic: On that same day Li Xiong died.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康二年正月丁巳，皇后見於太廟。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the first month of the second year of Xiankang, under Emperor Cheng of Jin, the empress appeared at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the first month of the second year of Xiankang, under Emperor Cheng of Jin, the empress made her appearance at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 其夕雨雹。

translations.literal: That evening hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening hail fell.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和三年八月，冀方大雪，人馬多凍死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Yonghe, under Emperor Mu of Jin, great snow in the Ji region; many men and horses froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Yonghe, under Emperor Mu of Jin, heavy snow struck the Ji region, and many men and horses froze to death.

sentences.zh: 永和五年六月，臨漳暴風震霆，雨雹大如升。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yonghe, violent wind and thunder in Linzhang; hail as large as a sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yonghe, violent wind and thunder shook Linzhang, and hailstones as large as a sheng fell.

sentences.zh: 永和十年五月，涼州雪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Yonghe, snow fell in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Yonghe, snow fell in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，桴罕護軍張瓘帥宗混等攻滅張祚，更立張曜靈弟玄靚。

translations.literal: The following year in the eighth month, Zhang Guan, Protector-General of Fuhan, led Zong Hun and others to attack and destroy Zhang Zuo, and installed Zhang Yaoling's younger brother Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year in the eighth month, Zhang Guan, Protector-General of Fuhan, led Zong Hun and others to attack and destroy Zhang Zuo, and set up Zhang Yaoling's younger brother Xuanjing in his place.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「夏雨雪，戒臣為亂。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When it rains and snows in summer, it warns that ministers will revolt."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When rain and snow fall in summer, it warns that ministers will rise in rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」永和十一年四月壬申朔，雪；

translations.literal: " On the renshen day, the first of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Yonghe, snow fell;
translations.idiomatic: " On the renshen day, the first of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Yonghe, snow fell;

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午，雷；

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month, thunder;
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month, thunder;

sentences.zh: 己未，雷。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day, thunder again.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day, thunder again.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼，母后稱制，政在大臣。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was young; the empress dowager ruled in his name, and government lay in the hands of the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was still a child; the empress dowager held regency, and power rested with the great ministers.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平二年正月，大雪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Shengping, under Emperor Mu of Jin, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Shengping, under Emperor Mu of Jin, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元二年四月己酉，雨雹；

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the fourth month of the second year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, hail fell;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the fourth month of the second year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, hail fell;

sentences.zh: 十二月，大雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼弱，政在將相。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was young and weak; government lay with the generals and chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was still a child, and power rested with the generals and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 太元十二年四月己醜，雨雹。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the fourth month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the fourth month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是時有事中州，兵役連歲。

translations.literal: At this time military operations were underway in the Central Plains, and corvée and campaigning continued year after year.
translations.idiomatic: At this time campaigns were underway in the Central Plains, and military service continued year after year.

sentences.zh: 太元二十年五月癸卯，上虞雨雹。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taiyuan, hail fell in Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taiyuan, hail fell in Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 太元二十一年四月丁亥，雨雹。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the fourth month of the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the fourth month of the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是時張夫人專幸，及帝暴崩，兆庶尤之。

translations.literal: At this time Lady Zhang enjoyed exclusive favor; when the emperor suddenly died, the multitude especially blamed her.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Lady Zhang held the emperor's exclusive favor, and when he died suddenly, the people laid the blame especially upon her.

sentences.zh: 太元二十一年十二月，連雪二十三日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, snow fell continuously for twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, snow fell without stop for twenty-three days.

sentences.zh: 是時嗣主幼沖，塚宰專政。

translations.literal: At this time the successor ruler was young; the chief minister monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the heir was still a child, and the chief minister held all power.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安二年三月乙卯，雨雹。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the third month of the second year of Long'an, under Emperor An of Jin, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the third month of the second year of Long'an, under Emperor An of Jin, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 是秋，王恭、殷仲堪入伐，終皆誅。

translations.literal: That autumn, Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan launched punitive campaigns; in the end both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan marched in force against the court; both were put to death in the end.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興二年十二月，酷寒過甚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, bitter cold was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, the cold was unusually severe.

sentences.zh: 是時桓玄篡位，政事煩苛，是其應也。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Xuan usurped the throne; government was vexatious and harsh—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Huan Xuan had seized the throne, and government had grown oppressive and harsh—the cold answered to this.

sentences.zh: 晉氏失在舒緩，玄則反之。

translations.literal: The Jin dynasty's fault lay in laxity and slack; Huan Xuan did the opposite.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had erred through laxity and indulgence; Huan Xuan swung to the opposite extreme.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「周衰無寒歲，秦滅無燠年。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "When Zhou declined there were no cold years; when Qin perished there were no warm years.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "When Zhou declined, no year was cold; when Qin fell, no year was warm.

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: " This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: " This is what he meant.

sentences.zh: 元興三年正月甲申，霰雪，又雷。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the first month of the third year of Yuanxing, sleet fell, and thunder followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the first month of the third year of Yuanxing, sleet fell, and thunder sounded as well.

sentences.zh: 雷霰不應同日，失節之應也。

translations.literal: Thunder and sleet should not occur on the same day—this was a response to loss of seasonal propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder and sleet ought not to come on the same day—it was a portent of the seasons thrown out of joint.

sentences.zh: 二月，義兵起，玄敗。

translations.literal: In the second month, righteous armies rose; Huan Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the loyalist armies rose, and Huan Xuan was defeated.

sentences.zh: 元興三年四月丙午，江陵雨雹。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the fourth month of the third year of Yuanxing, hail fell in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the fourth month of the third year of Yuanxing, hail fell in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 是時安帝蒙塵。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor An was in distress and exile.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor An was an emperor in exile.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉九年春，京都雨雹，溧陽、盱眙尤甚，傷牛馬，殺禽獸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year of Yuanjia, under Emperor Wen of Song, hail fell in the capital; Liyang and Xuyi were especially hard hit, injuring oxen and horses and killing birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year of Yuanjia, under Emperor Wen of Song, hail struck the capital, worst of all at Liyang and Xuyi, wounding cattle and horses and killing birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年三月，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 二十五虜寇青州。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei (Tuoba) barbarians raided Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei (Tuoba) barbarians invaded Qing province.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年正月，積雪冰寒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, accumulated snow and icy cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, deep snow and bitter ice cold prevailed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年五月，盱眙雨雹，大如雞卵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, hail fell in Xuyi, large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, hail fell at Xuyi, each stone as large as a hen's egg.

sentences.zh: 三十年，國家禍亂，兵革大起。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the state met calamity and disorder, and warfare rose on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the realm fell into catastrophe and rebellion, and war flared up on every side.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明元年十二月庚寅，大雪，平地二尺餘。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the twelfth month of the first year of Daming, under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, great snow fell, more than two chi deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the twelfth month of the first year of Daming, under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, heavy snow fell until level ground lay more than two chi deep.

sentences.zh: 明年，虜侵冀州，遣羽林軍北討。

translations.literal: The next year the barbarians invaded Ji province, and imperial guards were dispatched north to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year northern enemies invaded Ji province, and the palace guard was sent north to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始五年四月壬辰，京邑雨雹。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Taishi, under Emperor Ming, hail fell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Taishi, under Emperor Ming, hail fell in the capital.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年五月乙卯，京邑雨雹。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanhui, under the Later Deposed Emperor, hail fell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanhui, under the Later Deposed Emperor, hail fell in the capital.

sentences.zh: 雷震：

translations.literal: Thunder strikes:
translations.idiomatic: Thunder Strikes:

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初中，洛陽城東橋、洛水浮橋桓楹，同日三處俱震；

translations.literal: In the Jingchu era of Emperor Ming of Wei, bridge pillars at Luoyang's eastern city bridge and the Luo River pontoon bridge—three places on the same day were all struck;
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingchu era of Emperor Ming of Wei, thunder struck the bridge pillars at Luoyang's eastern city bridge and the Luo River pontoon bridge—all three within the same day;

sentences.zh: 尋又震西城上候風木飛烏。

translations.literal: Soon after it struck again the wind-watching wooden flying crow on the western city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward it struck the wind-vane wooden flying crow atop the western wall.

sentences.zh: 時勞役大起，帝尋晏駕。

translations.literal: At the time corvée labor rose on a grand scale; the emperor soon passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor was then levied on an enormous scale, and the emperor died soon after.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏八年夏，震宮門柱；

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year of Chiwu under Sun Quan of Wu, it struck the palace gate pillars;
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year of Chiwu, under Sun Quan of Wu, lightning struck the palace gate pillars;

sentences.zh: 又擊南津大橋桓楹。

translations.literal: It also struck the bridge pillars of the Nanjin Great Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: and also struck the pillars of the Nanjin Great Bridge.

sentences.zh: 孫亮建興元年十二月朔，大風震電；

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jianxing under Sun Liang, fierce wind, thunder, and lightning;
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jianxing, under Sun Liang, fierce winds brought thunder and lightning;

sentences.zh: 是月又雷雨。

translations.literal: That same month there was thunder and rain again.
translations.idiomatic: and later that month thunder and rain came again.

sentences.zh: 義同前說。

translations.literal: The meaning is the same as the earlier account.
translations.idiomatic: The omen carried the same meaning as before.

sentences.zh: 亮終廢。

translations.literal: Sun Liang was ultimately deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang was deposed in the end.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康六年十二月甲申朔，淮南郡震電。

translations.literal: On the first jiashen day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, thunder and lightning struck Huainan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the first jiashen day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, thunder and lightning appeared in Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 太康七年十二月己亥，毗陵雷電，南沙司鹽都尉戴亮以聞。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of the seventh year of Taikang, thunder and lightning struck Piling; Dai Liang, Superintendent of Salt for Nansha, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of the seventh year of Taikang, thunder and lightning struck Piling; Dai Liang, Superintendent of Salt at Nansha, made report of it.

sentences.zh: 太康十年十二月癸卯，廬江、建安雷電大雨。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of Taikang, thunder, lightning, and great rain struck Lujiang and Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of Taikang, thunder, lightning, and torrential rain struck Lujiang and Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝永嘉四年十月，震電。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, under Emperor Huai of Jin, thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, under Emperor Huai of Jin, thunder and lightning appeared.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌二年七月丙子朔，雷震太極殿柱。

translations.literal: On the first bingzi day of the seventh month of the second year of Yongchang, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, thunder struck the pillars of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On the first bingzi day of the seventh month of the second year of Yongchang, under Emperor Yuan of Jin, lightning struck the pillars of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 永昌二年十一月，會稽、吳郡雨震電。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Yongchang, rain, thunder, and lightning struck Kuaiji and Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Yongchang, rain fell amid thunder and lightning in Kuaiji and Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元五年六月甲寅，雷震含章殿四柱。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, thunder struck the four pillars of Hanzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, lightning struck the four pillars of Hanzhang Hall.

sentences.zh: 太元五年十二月，雷聲在南方。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Taiyuan, thunder sounded in the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Taiyuan, thunder was heard in the south.

sentences.zh: 太元十四年七月甲寅，震宣陽門西柱。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan, it struck the western pillar of Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan, lightning struck the western pillar of Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安二年九月壬辰，雨雷。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the ninth month of the second year of Long'an, under Emperor An of Jin, rain and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the ninth month of the second year of Long'an, under Emperor An of Jin, rain fell amid thunder.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興三年，永安皇后至自巴陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, the Empress of Yong'an arrived from Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, the Empress of Yong'an returned from Baling.

sentences.zh: 將設儀導入宮，天雷，震人馬各一俱殪。

translations.literal: As ceremonial escort was about to lead her into the palace, heaven's thunder struck; one man and one horse were each killed.
translations.idiomatic: As the ceremonial procession was about to conduct her into the palace, a thunderbolt fell, killing one man and one horse.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙四年十一月辛卯朔，西北疾風；

translations.literal: On the first xinmao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yixi, under Emperor An of Jin, a fierce wind blew from the northwest;
translations.idiomatic: On the first xinmao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yixi, under Emperor An of Jin, a fierce wind rose from the northwest;

sentences.zh: 癸醜，雷。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年六月丙寅，震太廟，破東鴟尾，徹壁柱。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yixi, it struck the Imperial Ancestral Temple, breaking the eastern roof ridge ornament and exposing the wall pillars.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yixi, lightning struck the Imperial Ancestral Temple, shattering the eastern chiwei roof ornament and tearing away the wall pillars.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年正月丙寅，雷；

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the first month of the sixth year of Yixi, thunder;
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the first month of the sixth year of Yixi, thunder sounded;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，又雪。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day, snow again.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, snow fell again.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年十二月壬辰，大雷。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Yixi, great thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Yixi, thunder rolled loudly.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年十一月甲戌，雷；

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yixi, thunder;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yixi, thunder sounded;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，又雷。

translations.literal: On the yihai day, thunder again.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, thunder sounded again.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉四年十一月癸醜，雷。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanjia, under Emperor Wen of Song, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanjia, under Emperor Wen of Song, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 元嘉五年六月丙寅，震太廟，破東鴟尾，徹壁柱。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia, it struck the Imperial Ancestral Temple, breaking the eastern roof ridge ornament and exposing the wall pillars.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia, lightning struck the Imperial Ancestral Temple, shattering the eastern chiwei roof ornament and tearing away the wall pillars.

sentences.zh: 元嘉六年正月丙寅，雷且雪。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the first month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, thunder and snow together.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the first month of the sixth year of Yuanjia, thunder sounded and snow fell together.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年十月丙子，雷。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the tenth month of the seventh year of Yuanjia, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the tenth month of the seventh year of Yuanjia, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年十二月庚辰，雷。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年十一月甲戌，雷且雪。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yuanjia, thunder and snow together.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yuanjia, thunder sounded and snow fell together.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十四年，震初寧陵口標，四破至地。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia, it struck the marker at the entrance to Chuning Mausoleum; all four pieces broke to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia, lightning struck the marker at the entrance to Chuning Mausoleum, shattering it in four pieces to the ground.

sentences.zh: 十七年，廢大將軍彭城王義康。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yi Kang, was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the Grand General, Prince of Pengcheng Yi Kang, was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 骨肉相害，自此始也。

translations.literal: Kinsmen harming one another began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The killing of kin within the imperial house began here.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年九月甲午，雷震。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the ninth month of the first year of Jinghe, under the Former Deposed Emperor, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the ninth month of the first year of Jinghe, under the Former Deposed Emperor, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年九月辛巳，雷震。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the ninth month of the second year of Taishi, under Emperor Ming, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the ninth month of the second year of Taishi, under Emperor Ming, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年十月辛卯，雷震。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day of the tenth month of the fourth year of Taishi, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the tenth month of the fourth year of Taishi, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年十一月癸卯朔，雷震。

translations.literal: On the first guimao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the first guimao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年十一月乙巳，雷震。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the eleventh month of the fifth year of Taishi, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eleventh month of the fifth year of Taishi, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年十一月庚午，雷。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month of the sixth year of Taishi, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month of the sixth year of Taishi, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年九月戊戌，雷。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, under the Later Deposed Emperor, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, under the Later Deposed Emperor, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年九月丁未，雷。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年九月戊午，雷震。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder struck.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年十月辛未，雷；

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the tenth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the tenth month of the third year of Yuanhui, thunder sounded;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，又雷。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, thunder again.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, thunder sounded again.

sentences.zh: 從帝升明三年二月二十四日丙申，震建陽門。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day, the bingshen day, of the second month of the third year of Shengming, under the Yielding Emperor, it struck Jianyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day, the bingshen day, of the second month of the third year of Shengming, under the Yielding Emperor, lightning struck Jianyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 鼓妖：

translations.literal: Drum prodigies:
translations.idiomatic: Drum Prodigies:

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康九年三月，有聲若牛，出許昌城。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Yuankang, under Emperor Hui of Jin, there was a sound like an ox emanating from outside Xuchang city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year of Yuankang, under Emperor Hui of Jin, a sound like the lowing of an ox was heard outside the walls of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廢太子，幽于許宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the crown prince was deposed and confined in the Xu palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the crown prince was deposed and imprisoned in the palace at Xu.

sentences.zh: 按《春秋》晉文公柩有聲如牛，劉向以為鼓妖。

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Wen of Jin's coffin made a sound like an ox; Liu Xiang held this to be a drum prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Wen of Jin's coffin gave forth a sound like an ox; Liu Xiang classified it as a drum prodigy.

sentences.zh: 其說曰：「聲如此，怒象也。

translations.literal: His explanation says: "A sound like this is an image of anger.
translations.idiomatic: His doctrine runs: "Such a sound is an image of wrath.

sentences.zh: 將有急怒之謀，以生兵甲之禍。

translations.literal: There will be plans of urgent anger, giving rise to the calamity of weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Violent counsels born of rage will soon follow, and with them the calamity of arms.

sentences.zh: 」此其類也。

translations.literal: " This is of that same kind.
translations.idiomatic: " This belongs to the same class.

sentences.zh: 明年，賈後遣黃門孫慮殺太子，擊以藥杵，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: The next year Empress Jia sent the Yellow Gate attendant Sun Lü to kill the crown prince, beating him with a medicine pestle until the sound was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Empress Jia sent the palace attendant Sun Lü to murder the crown prince, beating him with a medicine pestle until the blows could be heard outside.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻在曆陽，外營將軍鼓自鳴，如人弄鼓者。

translations.literal: When Su Jun was at Liyang, the general's drum in the outer camp sounded of itself, as if someone were beating it.
translations.idiomatic: While Su Jun held Liyang, the drum in the outer camp of the general's headquarters began to beat of its own accord, as though a man were striking it.

sentences.zh: 峻手自斫之，曰：「我鄉土時有此，則城空矣。

translations.literal: Su Jun himself hacked at it and said: "In my native place, when this happens, the city is emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun took an axe to it himself and said: "Back home, when this omen appears, the city stands empty.

sentences.zh: 」俄而作亂夷滅。

translations.literal: " Soon after he rebelled and was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he rose in rebellion and was utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 此聽不聰之罰，鼓妖先作也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for hearing not keen—the drum prodigy appeared first.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for deafness to counsel—the drum prodigy had sounded first.

sentences.zh: 石虎末，洛陽城西北九裏石牛在青石趺上，忽鳴喚，聲聞四十里。

translations.literal: At the end of Shi Hu's reign, a stone ox nine li northwest of Luoyang city, set on a bluestone pedestal, suddenly brayed, its voice heard for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Shi Hu's reign, a stone ox nine li northwest of Luoyang, mounted on a bluestone pedestal, suddenly bellowed, and the sound carried forty li.

sentences.zh: 虎遣人打落兩耳及尾，鐵釘釘四腳。

translations.literal: Hu sent men to knock off its two ears and tail, and iron nails were driven through its four legs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent men to break off its ears and tail and nail its four legs to the ground with iron spikes.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元十五年三月己酉朔，東北有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On the first jiyou day of the third month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, in the northeast there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the first jiyou day of the third month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a thunderous sound rolled from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說以為：「雷當托於雲，猶君托於臣。

translations.literal: Considering Liu Xiang's doctrine: "Thunder ought to rest upon clouds, just as the ruler rests upon his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Liu Xiang's account: "Thunder should lodge in the clouds, as the ruler lodges his trust in his ministers.

sentences.zh: 」無雲而雷，此君不恤下，下民將叛之象也。

translations.literal: " Thunder without clouds—this is an image of the ruler not caring for those below, and the people below about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: " Thunder without clouds signifies a ruler who does not care for his subjects—a portent that the people will turn against him.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩而天下漸亂，孫恩、桓玄交陵京邑。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the realm gradually fell into disorder; Sun En and Huan Xuan in succession overran the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death the realm slid into disorder, and Sun En and Huan Xuan in turn ravaged the capital.

sentences.zh: 吳興長城縣夏架山有石鼓，長丈餘，面徑三尺所，下有磐石為足，鳴則聲如金鼓，三吳有兵。

translations.literal: On Xiajia Mountain in Changcheng County, Wuxing, there is a stone drum more than one zhang long, its face about three chi across, with bedrock below serving as a base; when it sounds, the voice is like bronze drums, and the Three Wu region sees warfare.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiajia Mountain in Changcheng County of Wuxing there stands a stone drum more than one zhang long and about three chi across at the face, rooted on a bedrock pedestal. When it booms, the sound is like gongs and drums—and war comes to the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安中大鳴，後有孫靈秀之亂。

translations.literal: In the Long'an era under Emperor An of Jin it boomed greatly; afterward came the disorder of Sun Lingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Long'an era under Emperor An of Jin it sounded loudly, and afterward Sun Lingxiu rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魚孽：

translations.literal: Fish calamities:
translations.idiomatic: Fish Calamities:

sentences.zh: 魏齊王嘉平四年五月，有二魚集於武庫屋上。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jiaping, under the Prince of Qi of Wei, two fish gathered on the roof of the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jiaping, under the Prince of Qi of Wei, two fish appeared atop the armory roof.

sentences.zh: 此魚孽也。

translations.literal: This was a fish calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This was a fish calamity.

sentences.zh: 王肅曰：「魚生於淵，而亢於屋，介鱗之物，失其所也。

translations.literal: Wang Su said: "Fish are born in the deep, yet rise high upon a roof—creatures with scales and fins have lost their proper place."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "Fish belong in the depths, yet they climbed onto a rooftop—scaled creatures had lost their proper place."

sentences.zh: 邊將其殆有棄甲之變乎。

translations.literal: The frontier generals will perhaps suffer the disaster of casting off their armor.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the frontier generals were about to cast off their armor in defeat.

sentences.zh: 」後果有東關之敗。

translations.literal: " In the end there was indeed the defeat at Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end came the defeat at Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 幹寶又以為高貴鄉公兵禍之應。

translations.literal: Gan Bao also took it as the response to the military calamity of the Duke of Gaogui.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao also interpreted it as a portent of the military disaster that befell the Duke of Gaogui.

sentences.zh: 二說皆與班固旨同。

translations.literal: Both interpretations accord with Ban Gu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Both interpretations accord with Ban Gu's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康中，有鯉魚二見武庫屋上。

translations.literal: During the Taikang era of Emperor Wu of Jin, two carp appeared on the roof of the armory.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taikang era, under Emperor Wu of Jin, two carp were seen on the roof of the armory.

sentences.zh: 幹寶曰：「武庫兵府，魚有鱗甲，亦兵類也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The armory is the storehouse of arms; fish have scales and fins—they too belong to the class of arms."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "The armory is the storehouse of weapons, and fish with their scales belong to the same class."

sentences.zh: 魚既極陰，屋上太陽，魚見屋上，象至陰以兵革之禍幹太陽也。

translations.literal: Fish are utterly yin; the roof is yang; fish appearing on the roof images utmost yin using the calamity of arms to assail yang.
translations.idiomatic: Fish are utterly yin, the rooftop utterly yang—fish upon a roof signified utmost yin striking at yang through the calamity of war.

sentences.zh: 」至惠帝初，誅楊駿，廢太后，矢交館閣。

translations.literal: " By the beginning of Emperor Hui's reign, Yang Jun was executed, the empress dowager deposed, and arrows crossed between halls and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: " By the beginning of Emperor Hui's reign, Yang Jun had been executed, the empress dowager deposed, and arrows flew between palace halls.

sentences.zh: 元康末，賈後謗殺太子，尋亦誅廢。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuankang, Empress Jia slandered and killed the crown prince, and soon was herself executed and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuankang era, Empress Jia destroyed the crown prince through slander, and soon met execution and deposition herself.

sentences.zh: 十年間，母后之難再興，是其應也。

translations.literal: Within ten years the calamity of the empress dowager arose twice—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Within a decade, calamities involving the empress dowager arose twice—this was the corresponding manifestation.

sentences.zh: 自是禍亂構矣。

translations.literal: From this disaster and disorder took shape.
translations.idiomatic: From that point disorder and calamity took shape.

sentences.zh: 京房《易妖》曰：「魚去水，飛入道路，兵且作。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Omens of the Changes" says: "Fish leave the water and fly into the road—arms are about to be raised."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Omens of the Changes" says: "When fish leave the water and fly into the road, war is about to break out."

sentences.zh: 蝗蟲：

translations.literal: Locusts:
translations.idiomatic: Locusts:

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年七月，冀州大蝗，民饑。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, Ji Province suffered great locusts and the people starved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Huangchu, under Emperor Wen of Wei, locusts devastated Ji Province and the people faced famine.

sentences.zh: 案蔡邕說：「蝗者，在上貪苛之所致也。

translations.literal: According to Cai Yong's doctrine: "Locusts are produced by greed and harshness above."
translations.idiomatic: According to Cai Yong's doctrine: "Locusts arise from greed and harshness at the top."

sentences.zh: 」是時孫權歸從，帝因其有西陵之役，舉大眾襲之，權遂背叛。

translations.literal: " At this time Sun Quan had submitted; the emperor, because Quan had the Xiling campaign, raised a great host to attack him, and Quan then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time Sun Quan had submitted to the court. The emperor, taking advantage of Quan's involvement at Xiling, launched a great attack, and Quan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始十年六月，蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Taishi, under Emperor Wu of Jin, locusts appeared.

sentences.zh: 是時荀、賈任政，疾害公直。

translations.literal: At this time Xun and Jia held government and harmed the upright and impartial.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Xun and Jia clans held power and persecuted the upright.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉四年五月，大蝗，自幽、並、司、冀至於秦、雍，草木牛馬毛鬣皆盡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, great locusts from You, Bing, Si, and Ji as far as Qin and Yong stripped grass, trees, cattle, and horses of hair and mane entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, under Emperor Huai of Jin, locusts swept from You, Bing, Si, and Ji to Qin and Yong, stripping every blade of grass, every tree, and every hair from cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 是時天下兵亂，漁獵生民，存亡所系，唯司馬越、苟晞而已，而競為暴刻，經略無章。

translations.literal: At this time the empire was in military disorder, preying on the people for survival; what hung in the balance depended on Sima Yue and Gou Xi alone, yet they vied in cruelty and harshness, their strategy without order.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was torn by war, and the powerful preyed on the people. Survival hung on Sima Yue and Gou Xi alone, yet they vied in cruelty and governed without plan.

sentences.zh: 晉湣帝建興四年六月，大蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, great locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Jianxing, under Emperor Min of Jin, locusts appeared in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 去歲胡寇頻攻北地、馮翊，暐允等悉眾禦之。

translations.literal: In the previous year Hu raiders repeatedly attacked Beidi and Fufeng; Yin Guang and others mustered all their forces to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, barbarian raiders had repeatedly attacked Beidi and Fufeng, and Yin Guang and others had mustered every available force to resist.

sentences.zh: 是時又禦劉曜，為曜所破，西京遂潰。

translations.literal: At this time they again resisted Liu Yao, were defeated by Yao, and the western capital collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: They then faced Liu Yao again, were defeated, and the western capital fell.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十五年八月，兗州蝗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Taixuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, locusts in Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of Taixuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, locusts struck Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 是時丁零寇兗、豫，鮮卑逼河南，征戍不已。

translations.literal: At this time the Dingling raided Yan and Yu; the Xianbei pressed Henan; campaigns and garrisons never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Dingling raided Yan and Yu, the Xianbei pressed Henan, and campaigns and garrisons never ceased.

sentences.zh: 太元十六年五月，飛蝗從南來，集堂邑縣界，害苗稼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year of Taixuan, flying locusts came from the south, gathered at the border of Tangyi County, and harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year of Taixuan, flying locusts came from the south, gathered in Tangyi County, and destroyed the crops.

sentences.zh: 是年春，發取江州兵營甲士二千人家口六七千人，配護軍及東宮，後尋散亡殆盡；

translations.literal: That spring they drafted two thousand armored soldiers from Jiang Province military camps with six or seven thousand dependents, assigned to the Protector Army and the Eastern Palace, and soon nearly all scattered and perished;
translations.idiomatic: That spring the court drafted two thousand armored soldiers from Jiang Province camps, along with six or seven thousand dependents, and assigned them to the Protector Army and the Eastern Palace. Soon nearly all had scattered or perished;

sentences.zh: 又邊將連有征殺。

translations.literal: moreover frontier generals waged campaigns and killings in succession.
translations.idiomatic: while frontier generals waged one campaign and slaughter after another.

sentences.zh: 豕禍：

translations.literal: Pig disasters:
translations.idiomatic: Pig disasters:

sentences.zh: 吳孫皓寶鼎元年，野豕入右司馬丁奉營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu, a wild boar entered the camp of the Right Grand Marshal Ding Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding, under Sun Hao of Wu, a wild boar entered the camp of the Right Grand Marshal Ding Feng.

sentences.zh: 此豕禍也。

translations.literal: This was a pig disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This was a pig disaster.

sentences.zh: 後奉見遣攻谷陽，無功反，皓怒，斬其導軍。

translations.literal: Later Feng was sent to attack Guyang, returned without success, Hao was enraged, and beheaded his guide general.
translations.idiomatic: Later Feng was dispatched to attack Guyang, returned without success, and Hao in his rage beheaded Feng's guide general.

sentences.zh: 及舉大眾北出，奉及萬彧等相謂曰：「若至華里，不得不各自還也。

translations.literal: When he raised a great host to march north, Feng and Wan Yu and others said to one another: "If we reach Huali, we will have no choice but each to turn back."
translations.idiomatic: When Hao raised a great army to march north, Feng and Wan Yu and others said to one another: "If we reach Huali, each of us will have to turn back on our own."

sentences.zh: 」此謀泄，奉時雖已死，皓追討谷陽事，殺其子溫，家屬皆遠徙。

translations.literal: " This plot leaked out; though Feng had already died by then, Hao pursued the matter of Guyang, killed his son Wen, and all his family were exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: " The plot leaked out. Though Feng was already dead, Hao pursued the Guyang affair, killed his son Wen, and exiled the entire family.

sentences.zh: 豕禍之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to the pig disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of the pig disaster.

sentences.zh: 龔遂曰：「山野之獸，來入宮室，宮室將空。

translations.literal: Gong Sui said: "Wild beasts of the mountains and fields entering the palace chambers—the palace chambers are about to stand empty."
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sui said: "When wild beasts of mountain and field enter the palace, the palace is about to stand empty."

sentences.zh: 」又其象也。

translations.literal: " This too was its image.
translations.idiomatic: " That too was its portent.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉中，壽春城內有豕生兩頭而不活。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia era of Emperor Huai of Jin, within Shouchun city a sow gave birth to a piglet with two heads that did not live.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongjia era, under Emperor Huai of Jin, a sow in Shouchun gave birth to a two-headed piglet that did not survive.

sentences.zh: 周馥取而觀之。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu took it and examined it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu took it and examined it.

sentences.zh: 時通數者竊謂曰：「夫豕，北方之畜，胡、狄象也。

translations.literal: A man skilled in numbers privately said to him: "The pig is a creature of the north—the image of the Hu and Di."
translations.idiomatic: A man skilled in divination whispered to him: "The pig is a northern creature—the image of the Hu and Di barbarians."

sentences.zh: 兩頭者，無上也。

translations.literal: Two heads mean no ruler above.
translations.idiomatic: Two heads signify the absence of a supreme ruler.

sentences.zh: 生而死，不遂也。

translations.literal: Born yet dead means it will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Born yet dead means the endeavor will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，勿生專利之謀，將自致傾覆也。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seemed to say: do not harbor schemes for exclusive profit, or you will bring ruin upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent seemed to say: do not harbor schemes for selfish gain, or you will bring ruin upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 」周馥不悟，遂欲迎天子，令諸侯，俄為元帝所敗。

translations.literal: " Zhou Fu did not understand, then wished to welcome the Son of Heaven and command the feudal lords, and soon was defeated by Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Fu failed to understand. He then sought to welcome the Son of Heaven and command the regional lords, and was soon defeated by Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 是其應也。

translations.literal: This was its response.
translations.idiomatic: This was the corresponding manifestation.

sentences.zh: 石勒亦尋渡淮，百姓死者十八九。

translations.literal: Shi Le also soon crossed the Huai; eight or nine out of ten common people died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le soon crossed the Huai as well, and eight or nine people in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝鹹和六年六月，錢塘民家豭豕生兩子，皆人面，如胡人狀，其身猶豕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a boar at a household in Qiantang gave birth to two young, all with human faces like the appearance of Hu people, their bodies still those of pigs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xianhe, under Emperor Cheng of Jin, a boar in Qiantang gave birth to two piglets with human faces like those of barbarians, their bodies still those of swine.

sentences.zh: 京房《易妖》曰：「豕生人頭豕身者，邑且亂亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Omens of the Changes" says: "When a pig gives birth to a human head and pig body, the town will soon fall into disorder and perish."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Omens of the Changes" says: "When a pig bears offspring with human heads and swine bodies, the town will soon fall into chaos and ruin."

sentences.zh: 」此豭豕而產，異之甚者也。

translations.literal: " This boar giving birth was an extreme of strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: " For a boar to give such birth was strangeness in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十年四月，京都有豕，一頭二身八足。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taixuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, in the capital there was a pig with one head, two bodies, and eight legs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Taixuan, under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a pig with one head, two bodies, and eight legs appeared in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，京都民家豕產子，一頭二身八足。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a household pig in the capital gave birth to young with one head, two bodies, and eight legs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year a household sow in the capital gave birth to piglets with one head, two bodies, and eight legs.

sentences.zh: 並與建武同妖也。

translations.literal: Both were the same prodigy as in Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Both matched the prodigy of the Jianwu era.

sentences.zh: 是後宰相沈酗，不恤朝政，近慣用事，漸亂國綱，至於大壞也。

translations.literal: After this the chief ministers were sunk in drink, heedless of court government; favorites monopolized power, gradually throwing the state's bonds into disorder until great ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the chief ministers drowned themselves in drink and neglected government, while favorites monopolized power, gradually unraveling the state until total ruin came.

sentences.zh: 黑眚黑祥：

translations.literal: Black disasters and black portents:
translations.idiomatic: Black disasters and black omens:

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉五年十二月，黑氣四塞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, black qi blocked all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Yongjia, under Emperor Huai of Jin, black vapor filled the horizon on every side.

sentences.zh: 近黑祥也。

translations.literal: This approached a black portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a black omen.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十六年三月，幸京口。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, he visited Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen of Song visited Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 有黑氣暴起，佔有兵。

translations.literal: Black qi rose violently; divination indicated arms.
translations.idiomatic: Black vapor rose violently, and diviners read it as a portent of war.

sentences.zh: 明年，虜南寇至瓜步，飲馬于江。

translations.literal: The following year the barbarians raided south to Guabu and watered their horses in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The following year northern enemies raided south as far as Guabu and watered their horses in the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 火沴水：

translations.literal: Fire harming water:
translations.idiomatic: Fire injuring water:

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年六月，任城、魯國池水皆赤如血。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, the pool waters of Rencheng and Lu Kingdom all turned red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taikang, under Emperor Wu of Jin, the pool waters of Rencheng and Lu turned red as blood.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，近火沴水也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's doctrine, this approached fire harming water.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's doctrine, this approached fire injuring water.

sentences.zh: 聽之不聰之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for hearing that is not keen.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for failure of hearing.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「淫于色，賢人潛，國家危，厥異水流赤。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "Dissolute in lust, worthy men in hiding, the state in peril—its anomaly is water flowing red."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When the ruler is dissolute in lust, worthy men withdraw, the state faces peril, and water flows red."

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平三年二月，涼州城東池中有火；

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, fire appeared in the eastern pool of Liang Province city;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Shengping, under Emperor Mu of Jin, fire appeared in the eastern pool of Liang Province;

sentences.zh: 四年四月，姑臧澤水中又有火。

translations.literal: in the fourth month of the fourth year, fire again appeared in the waters of the Guzang marsh.
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth month of the fourth year, fire appeared again in the waters of the Guzang marsh.

sentences.zh: 此火沴水之妖也。

translations.literal: This was the prodigy of fire harming water.
translations.idiomatic: This was a prodigy of fire injuring water.

sentences.zh: 明年，張天錫殺中護軍張邕。

translations.literal: The following year Zhang Tianxi killed the Central Protector Army Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Tianxi killed the Central Protector Army commander Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 邕，執政臣也。

translations.literal: Yong was a minister who held government.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a minister who held real power.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興二年十月，錢塘臨平湖水赤。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, the waters of Linping Lake in Qiantang turned red.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Yuanxing, under Emperor An of Jin, the waters of Linping Lake in Qiantang turned red.

sentences.zh: 桓玄諷吳郡使言開除，以為己瑞。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan prompted the Wu commandery envoy to report it as an auspicious opening, taking it as his own omen of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan prompted the Wu commandery envoy to report it as an auspicious sign, treating it as his own blessing.

sentences.zh: 俄而玄敗。

translations.literal: Soon Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xuan met defeat.
